title: Finite type domains have regular opens from residue-field finite models
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Suppose that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ and every finite purely inseparable field extension $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime; def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], with $R\to L$ the residue-field map followed by the given extension, there is an $R$-subalgebra $B\subseteq L$ which is finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], whose fractions $b/c$ ($b,c\in B$, $c\ne0$) exhaust $L$, and for which $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] contains a nonempty open subset $U$ such that $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every $\mathfrak q\in U$. Then every finite type $R$-algebra $S$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] which is a nonzero integral domain has a nonempty open subset $V$ of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ such that $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local for every $\mathfrak q\in V$.

proof.text: Fix a finite type domain $S$ over $R$, generated by $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ over $R$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Put $\mathfrak p=\ker(R\to S)$, a prime because $S$ is a domain, and let $K$ be the field of fractions of $S$. The residue field $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ embeds into $K$: its element $(r+\mathfrak p)/(u+\mathfrak p)$, $u\notin\mathfrak p$, maps to the fraction of the images of $r,u$ in $S$. In $R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, two such fractions $r/u$ and $r'/u'$ are equal exactly when $ru'-r'u\in\mathfrak p$: multiplying by the unit denominators reduces this to $(ru'-r'u)/1\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, and the localization equivalence and primality give that condition exactly. Their images in $K$ are equal exactly when $ru'-r'u$ maps to zero in $S$, which is the same condition since $\ker(R\to S)=\mathfrak p$. Thus the formula is well-defined and injective; the fraction formulas for addition and multiplication show it is a field homomorphism. Every element of $K$ is a quotient of polynomials in the $s_i$ over the image of $R$, so $K=k(s_1,\ldots,s_n)$ is finitely generated as a field over $k$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-make-separable] to the finitely generated field extension $K/k$. Obtain a commutative square $k\to L\to K'$, $k\to K\to K'$ in which $L/k$ and $K'/K$ are finite purely inseparable and $K'/L$ is separable. Identify the fields with their images in $K'$; field homomorphisms are injective because their kernels are proper ideals in fields. This gives exactly a finite purely inseparable extension of the specified residue field to which the hypothesis on $R$ applies.

proof.text: Choose the finite $R$-subalgebra $B$ of $L$ supplied by the hypothesis. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian], and its fraction field identifies with $L$. Form the image $C$ of $B\otimes_R S\to K′$, mapping $b\otimes s$ to the product of their images. This is a subalgebra of a field, hence a nonzero domain. Base change of the finite type algebra $S/R$, followed by passage to the image, makes $C$ finite type over $B$. Since $B$ is finite over $R$, it is finite type over $R$; transitivity makes $C$ finite type over $R$, and restriction of scalars makes it finite type over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. The inclusion of $S$ into $C$ is injective because its composite with $C\hookrightarrow K′$ is the injection $S\hookrightarrow K\hookrightarrow K′$. The map $B\to C$ is injective because its composite into $K′$ factors through the injections $B\hookrightarrow L\hookrightarrow K′$.

proof.text: Let $e:\operatorname{Frac}(B)\simeq L$ be the canonical equivalence, fixing $B$. The injection $C\hookrightarrow K′$ extends uniquely to an injection $j:\operatorname{Frac}(C)\hookrightarrow K′$. The induced maps from $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ to $K′$ agree: after precomposition with $B\to\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ both send $b$ to its specified image in $K′$, and uniqueness of fraction-field extensions gives equality. Transfer the separability of $K′/L$ along $e$, then restrict it along $j$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Explicitly, the image of a finitely generated intermediate field under $j$ is finitely generated, since images of its finite generators generate it. This image is separably generated by the hypothesis. Pull its transcendence basis and the algebraic separability back along the field equivalence. Changing the base field along $e$ likewise transports algebraic independence, maximality of a transcendence basis, and algebraic separability. Thus the exact fraction-field map induced by $B\to C$ is separable.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-j0-separable-finite-type-ascent] to B to C. The base B is Noetherian, both rings are domains, and the map is injective finite type by step 3. The induced fraction-field extension is separable by step 4, and the required regular open of B was chosen from the hypothesis. Thus C has a nonempty regular open. Apply [lem-exc-j0-finite-type-domain-descent] to the injective finite type map S to C, using the Noetherianity of S from step 1. Conclude that S has a nonempty regular open.
